paragraphs.title: The Command to Keep and Write

easy.question: Who commanded the people to keep all the commandments?
answers: Moses and the elders of Israel
The king of Israel
The priests alone
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people to keep all the commandments.

easy.question: What were the people to do with the stones?
answers: Break them
Set them up and plaster them
Bury them
easy.explanation: The people were commanded to set up large stones and plaster them.

easy.question: When were the Israelites commanded to write on the stones?
answers: Before the Exodus from Egypt
Before the giving of the Law
When they crossed the Jordan
easy.explanation: The verse says to write on the stones when they crossed the Jordan, after entering the land.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Cross the Jordan, set up the stones, plaster them, and write on them
Write on the stones, cross the Jordan, and then set them up
Set up the stones in the wilderness and return to Egypt
medium.explanation: First they cross the Jordan, then set up and plaster the stones, and finally write on them.

medium.question: In the phrase “plaster them with plaster,” what does “plaster” mean?
answers: Paint them red
Cover them with a layer of plaster
Arrange them in the soil
medium.explanation: The stones were to be coated or covered with plaster before the words of the Law were written on them.

medium.question: What was the purpose of writing the words of the Law on the stones?
answers: To decorate the road
To mark the edge of the wilderness
As part of the people’s entrance into the land God had promised to give them
medium.explanation: The verse connects the writing with entering the land God was giving Israel, a land flowing with milk and honey.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the stones were set up immediately after the Jordan was crossed?
answers: They served as a visible reminder connecting the crossing of the Jordan with obeying the words of the Law
They were meant to hide the crossing place
They served as houses for the people
challenge.explanation: Setting up the stones after the crossing and writing the Law on them connected entering the land with the duty to keep the Law.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “all the words of this law” emphasize?
answers: That only one commandment was to be written
That the whole Law was to be written, not merely a small part of it
That there was no need to keep the Law
challenge.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that the entire message of the Law was to be written, not just one idea or commandment.

challenge.question: What does the connection between “so that” and the description of the land teach us?
answers: That the land would be given to Israel only if they found water there
That the writing was meant to delay their entrance into the land
That the writing was connected with fulfilling God’s promise to bring Israel into the land
challenge.explanation: The phrase “so that” expresses purpose, and the following words connect that purpose with entering the land God promised to the ancestors.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that the stones were set up immediately after the Jordan was crossed?
answers: They served as a visible reminder connecting the crossing of the Jordan with obeying the words of the Law
They were meant to hide the crossing place
They served as houses for the people
questions.explanation: Setting up the stones after the crossing and writing the Law on them connected entering the land with the duty to keep the Law.

questions.question: What does the phrase “all the words of this law” emphasize?
answers: That only one commandment was to be written
That the whole Law was to be written, not merely a small part of it
That there was no need to keep the Law
questions.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that the entire message of the Law was to be written, not just one idea or commandment.

questions.question: What does the connection between “so that” and the description of the land teach us?
answers: That the land would be given to Israel only if they found water there
That the writing was meant to delay their entrance into the land
That the writing was connected with fulfilling God’s promise to bring Israel into the land
questions.explanation: The phrase “so that” expresses purpose, and the following words connect that purpose with entering the land God promised to the ancestors.

paragraphs.title: Building the Altar and Rejoicing Before the Lord

easy.question: What were the Israelites commanded to set up after crossing the Jordan?
answers: The stones
The tabernacle
The city wall
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to set up the stones after crossing the Jordan.

easy.question: On which mountain were they commanded to set up the stones?
answers: Mount Gerizim
Mount Ebal
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The stones were to be set up on Mount Ebal.

easy.question: What were they to write on the stones?
answers: The names of the leaders
The Ten Commandments only
All the words of this Law
easy.explanation: The verse says to write all the words of the Law on the stones.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the actions described in these verses?
answers: Set up stones, build an altar, offer sacrifices, and write the Law
Write the Law, eat, cross the Jordan, and build an altar
Build an altar, cross the Jordan, write the Law, and set up stones
medium.explanation: First they cross the Jordan and set up stones; then they build an altar, offer sacrifices, eat, and write the Law on the stones.

medium.question: Why were they commanded to build the altar with whole stones and not use an iron tool on them?
answers: So the stones would be easy to carry
So the altar would be built from stones that had not been worked with iron
So the iron could be saved for war
medium.explanation: The verses emphasize that the altar was to be built from whole stones, without using an iron tool.

medium.question: In the phrase “write all the words of this law very plainly,” what does “very plainly” mean?
answers: Bury them deeply
Decorate them with colors
Present them clearly
medium.explanation: In this context, “very plainly” means that the words were to be presented in a clear and understandable way.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the command to write all the words of the Law on the stones?
answers: The Law was meant to be public and remembered by the people
Only the priests were allowed to know the Law
The writing was meant only to decorate the altar
challenge.explanation: Writing the Law on stones in a public place emphasized the importance of making it known and remembering it among the people.

challenge.question: What detail distinguishes the burnt offerings from the peace offerings in these verses?
answers: The burnt offerings were eaten there, but the peace offerings were not
The burnt offerings were offered to the Lord, while the people ate the peace offerings and rejoiced
The peace offerings were made without an altar
challenge.explanation: The burnt offerings are described as being offered to the Lord, while the peace offerings were eaten with rejoicing before Him.

challenge.question: What idea connects building the altar with eating and rejoicing before the Lord?
answers: Worship of the Lord includes both sacrifice and shared joy
Joy takes the place of keeping the Law
The eating was meant to hide the stones
challenge.explanation: The verses connect worship at the altar with a peace-offering meal and rejoicing before the Lord.

questions.question: What can we infer from the command to write all the words of the Law on the stones?
answers: The Law was meant to be public and remembered by the people
Only the priests were allowed to know the Law
The writing was meant only to decorate the altar
questions.explanation: Writing the Law on stones in a public place emphasized the importance of making it known and remembering it among the people.

questions.question: What detail distinguishes the burnt offerings from the peace offerings in these verses?
answers: The burnt offerings were eaten there, but the peace offerings were not
The burnt offerings were offered to the Lord, while the people ate the peace offerings and rejoiced
The peace offerings were made without an altar
questions.explanation: The burnt offerings are described as being offered to the Lord, while the peace offerings were eaten with rejoicing before Him.

questions.question: What idea connects building the altar with eating and rejoicing before the Lord?
answers: Worship of the Lord includes both sacrifice and shared joy
Joy takes the place of keeping the Law
The eating was meant to hide the stones
questions.explanation: The verses connect worship at the altar with a peace-offering meal and rejoicing before the Lord.

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s People and Accepting the Commandments

easy.question: Who spoke to all Israel?
answers: Moses and the Levitical priests
Joshua and the elders
The king of Israel and the people
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel.

easy.question: Whose people had Israel become on that day?
answers: Moses’
The Lord their God’s
The Levitical priests’
easy.explanation: The verse says, “This day you have become the people of the Lord your God.”

easy.question: What were Israel commanded to do regarding the Lord’s commandments?
answers: Write them on the stones
Teach them only to the priests
Obey the voice of the Lord and keep His commandments and statutes
easy.explanation: Verse 10 commands Israel to obey the Lord’s voice and keep His commandments and statutes.

medium.question: In the phrase “Take heed and hearken, O Israel,” what does “take heed” mean?
answers: Move away
Pay close attention
Rejoice
medium.explanation: “Take heed” means to pay close attention and listen seriously; the following words reinforce this meaning.

medium.question: What is the connection between Israel becoming the Lord’s people and the command in the next verse?
answers: Because they are His people, they must obey His voice and keep His commandments
Because they are His people, they are free from the commandments
Because they are His people, only the priests must obey Him
medium.explanation: The verses connect being the Lord’s people with the responsibility to obey His voice and keep His commandments.

medium.question: What is the order of ideas in these verses?
answers: Keeping the commandments, then listening, and finally becoming the Lord’s people
Becoming the Lord’s people, then obeying His voice, and finally keeping His commandments
Obeying the Lord’s voice, then becoming His people, and finally accepting the commandments
medium.explanation: First Israel is declared to have become the Lord’s people; afterward they are commanded to obey His voice and keep His commandments and statutes.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the repetition of the word “today” in these verses?
answers: The matters applied only to one day and were not binding afterward
The commandments were given only to the priests
The occasion was a significant moment of renewed commitment
challenge.explanation: The emphasis on “this day” marks an important time when Israel became the Lord’s people and committed themselves to obeying Him.

challenge.question: Why does the verse say both “obey the voice of the Lord” and “keep His commandments”?
answers: To emphasize that listening alone is not enough; action is also required
To distinguish Israel from the priests
To say that listening and obeying are contradictory commandments
challenge.explanation: The verse presents two complementary steps: listening to the command and then carrying it out.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the message was addressed to the entire nation rather than a small group?
answers: The phrase “the Levitical priests”
The phrase “to all Israel”
The phrase “which I command you”
challenge.explanation: The phrase “to all Israel” makes clear that the message and its requirements were directed to the whole nation.

questions.question: What can we infer from the repetition of the word “today” in these verses?
answers: The matters applied only to one day and were not binding afterward
The commandments were given only to the priests
The occasion was a significant moment of renewed commitment
questions.explanation: The emphasis on “this day” marks an important time when Israel became the Lord’s people and committed themselves to obeying Him.

questions.question: Why does the verse say both “obey the voice of the Lord” and “keep His commandments”?
answers: To emphasize that listening alone is not enough; action is also required
To distinguish Israel from the priests
To say that listening and obeying are contradictory commandments
questions.explanation: The verse presents two complementary steps: listening to the command and then carrying it out.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the message was addressed to the entire nation rather than a small group?
answers: The phrase “the Levitical priests”
The phrase “to all Israel”
The phrase “which I command you”
questions.explanation: The phrase “to all Israel” makes clear that the message and its requirements were directed to the whole nation.

easy.question: Who commanded the people on that day?
answers: Moses
Joshua
The Levites
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “And Moses charged the people the same day.”

easy.question: On which mountain were the tribes to stand to bless the people?
answers: Mount Ebal
Mount Gerizim
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that the tribes were to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people.

easy.question: Which tribes were to stand for the curse on Mount Ebal?
answers: Simeon, Levi, and Judah
Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin
Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali
easy.explanation: Verse 13 lists Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali as standing for the curse.

medium.question: What was the difference between the tribes’ roles on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal?
answers: On Mount Gerizim they blessed, and on Mount Ebal they stood for the curse
On Mount Gerizim they stood for the curse, and on Mount Ebal they blessed
Everyone blessed on both mountains
medium.explanation: The verses divide the tribes into two groups: one for blessing on Mount Gerizim and one for the curse on Mount Ebal.

medium.question: In the phrase “to bless the people,” what does “bless” mean?
answers: Judge the people
Wish the people well and pronounce a blessing
Count the people
medium.explanation: To bless means to wish someone good; here the tribes stood before the people to pronounce a blessing.

medium.question: How were the Levites to speak to Israel?
answers: Quietly
In writing
With a loud voice
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says that the Levites were to speak with a loud voice, clearly and forcefully.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that six tribes are listed on Mount Gerizim and six on Mount Ebal?
answers: All twelve tribes of Israel were divided into two equal groups
Only half of the tribes participated
The tribes were divided according to age
challenge.explanation: Six tribes are named on each mountain, indicating that all twelve tribes participated in an equal division.

challenge.question: What special role did the Levites have according to the final verse?
answers: To stand only on Mount Ebal
To answer and speak the words to all Israel in a loud voice
To bless alone on Mount Gerizim
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the Levites spoke to every Israelite, rather than merely standing on one of the mountains.

challenge.question: Which detail about the tribe of Levi is accurate according to these verses?
answers: Levi was listed among the tribes standing for the curse
Levi was not mentioned at all
Levi was listed among the tribes for the blessing, and the Levites also spoke the words
challenge.explanation: Levi appears in the list of tribes on Mount Gerizim, while verse 14 describes the Levites speaking the words aloud.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that six tribes are listed on Mount Gerizim and six on Mount Ebal?
answers: All twelve tribes of Israel were divided into two equal groups
Only half of the tribes participated
The tribes were divided according to age
questions.explanation: Six tribes are named on each mountain, indicating that all twelve tribes participated in an equal division.

questions.question: What special role did the Levites have according to the final verse?
answers: To stand only on Mount Ebal
To answer and speak the words to all Israel in a loud voice
To bless alone on Mount Gerizim
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the Levites spoke to every Israelite, rather than merely standing on one of the mountains.

questions.question: Which detail about the tribe of Levi is accurate according to these verses?
answers: Levi was listed among the tribes standing for the curse
Levi was not mentioned at all
Levi was listed among the tribes for the blessing, and the Levites also spoke the words
questions.explanation: Levi appears in the list of tribes on Mount Gerizim, while verse 14 describes the Levites speaking the words aloud.

easy.question: What act is called “cursed” in verse 15?
answers: Making a carved or molten image
Honoring one’s parents
Helping a blind person
easy.explanation: The verse curses anyone who makes a carved or molten image and places it secretly.

easy.question: Who says “Amen” after each warning?
answers: The priests alone
All the people
The elders of the city alone
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly say, “And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.”

easy.question: What is a person cursed for in verse 16?
answers: Hiding an image
Moving a boundary marker
Treating his father or mother with contempt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother.”

medium.question: Which act appears immediately after the prohibition against making a carved or molten image?
answers: Making a blind person lose the way
Treating one’s father or mother with contempt
Moving a neighbor’s boundary marker
medium.explanation: Verse 15 mentions the image, and verse 16 then speaks of treating one’s father or mother with contempt.

medium.question: In the phrase “removeth his neighbour’s landmark,” what does it mean?
answers: Asks his neighbor for forgiveness
Protects his neighbor’s property
Moves the boundary of his neighbor’s property
medium.explanation: The phrase describes changing or moving a boundary marker, thereby violating a neighbor’s property rights.

medium.question: Why is making a blind person lose the way included among the cursed acts?
answers: Because it harms someone who depends on others for help
Because a blind person is not allowed to walk on the road
Because the road belongs only to the king
medium.explanation: Misleading a blind person exploits his vulnerability and may cause serious harm, making it a grave wrongdoing.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the list includes both idol worship and harming other people?
answers: The Law connects faithfulness to God with moral behavior
Only idol worship is considered a sin
Harming others is allowed if it is done secretly
challenge.explanation: The list teaches that worship of God is inseparable from honoring parents, respecting others’ property, and helping the vulnerable.

challenge.question: What is the special significance of the phrase “and puts it in a secret place” in verse 15?
answers: The act is permitted if no one sees it
Hiding the act does not remove its seriousness
The people do not need to know about it
challenge.explanation: Even if the image is made and placed secretly, the Law still condemns the act, and all the people affirm this by saying “Amen.”

challenge.question: Why is making a blind person lose the way especially serious?
answers: Because every road is sacred
Because a blind person always travels alone
Because the person depends on guidance and cannot easily tell whether he has been misled
challenge.explanation: A blind person depends on others for directions and cannot see dangers or easily check whether he has been deceived.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that the list includes both idol worship and harming other people?
answers: The Law connects faithfulness to God with moral behavior
Only idol worship is considered a sin
Harming others is allowed if it is done secretly
questions.explanation: The list teaches that worship of God is inseparable from honoring parents, respecting others’ property, and helping the vulnerable.

questions.question: What is the special significance of the phrase “and puts it in a secret place” in verse 15?
answers: The act is permitted if no one sees it
Hiding the act does not remove its seriousness
The people do not need to know about it
questions.explanation: Even if the image is made and placed secretly, the Law still condemns the act, and all the people affirm this by saying “Amen.”

questions.question: Why is making a blind person lose the way especially serious?
answers: Because every road is sacred
Because a blind person always travels alone
Because the person depends on guidance and cannot easily tell whether he has been misled
questions.explanation: A blind person depends on others for directions and cannot see dangers or easily check whether he has been deceived.

paragraphs.title: Protecting the Vulnerable and the Sanctity of Family

easy.question: Who is called “cursed” in verse 19?
answers: Anyone who perverts the judgment of the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Anyone who fails to honor his parents
Anyone who fails to bring an offering
easy.explanation: The verse warns against anyone who perverts the judgment of the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.

easy.question: What does all the people say after each warning?
answers: Blessed
Amen
We will go
easy.explanation: At the end of each verse, all the people say, “Amen.”

easy.question: With whom is it forbidden to lie in verse 21?
answers: With one’s sister
With one’s mother-in-law
With any beast
easy.explanation: Verse 21 says, “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast.”

medium.question: What is the first subject mentioned in this list of warnings?
answers: Doing justice for the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
The prohibition against lying with a beast
The prohibition against lying with one’s mother-in-law
medium.explanation: The list begins with a warning against perverting the judgment of the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.

medium.question: In the phrase “perverteth the judgment of the stranger,” what does “perverteth” mean?
answers: Teaches the stranger the laws of justice
Distorts or corrupts the stranger’s legal rights
Invites the stranger to court
medium.explanation: “Perverteth” means to distort or turn away from justice; the context concerns denying the stranger a fair judgment.

medium.question: What do the warnings in verses 20–23 have in common?
answers: They all concern business law
They all concern sacrificial worship
They all concern forbidden sexual relationships
medium.explanation: These verses prohibit relations with one’s father’s wife, a beast, one’s sister, and one’s mother-in-law.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between verse 19 and verses 20–23?
answers: Verse 19 concerns social and legal responsibility, while the other verses concern forbidden relationships
Verse 19 is a blessing, while the other verses are additional blessings
Verse 19 concerns only priests, while the other verses concern only kings
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 deals with protecting the vulnerable and administering justice, while verses 20–23 concern forbidden sexual relationships.

challenge.question: Which specific detail is stated about the sister in verse 22?
answers: Only a sister on the father’s side is included
The prohibition includes a sister who is the daughter of one’s father or mother
Only a married sister is included
challenge.explanation: The verse includes both possibilities: a sister who is the daughter of one’s father or the daughter of one’s mother.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the repeated words “And all the people shall say, Amen”?
answers: The people did not hear the declarations
The warnings were spoken only in secret
The people publicly approved and agreed with what was said
challenge.explanation: The repeated response of all the people, “Amen,” expresses public acceptance of the warnings and the obligations they present.

questions.question: What is the main difference between verse 19 and verses 20–23?
answers: Verse 19 concerns social and legal responsibility, while the other verses concern forbidden relationships
Verse 19 is a blessing, while the other verses are additional blessings
Verse 19 concerns only priests, while the other verses concern only kings
questions.explanation: Verse 19 deals with protecting the vulnerable and administering justice, while verses 20–23 concern forbidden sexual relationships.

questions.question: Which specific detail is stated about the sister in verse 22?
answers: Only a sister on the father’s side is included
The prohibition includes a sister who is the daughter of one’s father or mother
Only a married sister is included
questions.explanation: The verse includes both possibilities: a sister who is the daughter of one’s father or the daughter of one’s mother.

questions.question: What can we understand from the repeated words “And all the people shall say, Amen”?
answers: The people did not hear the declarations
The warnings were spoken only in secret
The people publicly approved and agreed with what was said
questions.explanation: The repeated response of all the people, “Amen,” expresses public acceptance of the warnings and the obligations they present.

easy.question: Who is called “cursed” in verse 24?
answers: Anyone who strikes his neighbor secretly
Anyone who helps the poor
Anyone who brings an offering
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly.”

easy.question: What does all the people do after the curse is spoken?
answers: Remain silent
Say “Amen”
Leave the city
easy.explanation: At the end of both verses, all the people say, “Amen.”

easy.question: What was the bribe taken for in verse 25?
answers: To build a house
To judge fairly
To slay an innocent person
easy.explanation: The verse describes someone taking a bribe in order to kill an innocent person.

medium.question: What do the acts described in verses 24 and 25 have in common?
answers: Both involve harming human life or justice
Both involve helping another person
In both cases the people punish the sinner
medium.explanation: Both verses condemn serious harm to a person: striking someone secretly or causing the death of an innocent person.

medium.question: In the phrase “taketh reward to slay,” what is a “reward”?
answers: A holiday gift
Money or a benefit given to influence an action
A punishment imposed by a court
medium.explanation: The context shows that the reward is a payment or benefit intended to induce someone to carry out the harmful act.

medium.question: What is the connection between taking the bribe and harming the person in verse 25?
answers: The bribe was taken after the harm was complete
The bribe was intended to prevent all harm
The bribe served as the reason or payment for carrying out the harm
medium.explanation: The verse connects taking the bribe with killing an innocent person, showing that the bribe led to the act of violence.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “an innocent person” mean in verse 25?
answers: A person who is not guilty and does not deserve punishment
A person who has washed his hands
Blood that has been washed with water
challenge.explanation: An innocent person is someone who is not guilty and whose harm or death is unjustified.

challenge.question: Why does the people say “Amen” after each curse?
answers: To ask forgiveness for the act
To publicly agree that the act deserves condemnation
To announce that the offender has been found
challenge.explanation: Saying “Amen” expresses agreement with the curse and acceptance of the moral principle it represents.

challenge.question: What detail do the two verses share, although each describes it differently?
answers: In both cases the offender acts on behalf of a court
In both cases the act is done for the poor
In both cases a person suffers serious harm, and the act is presented as deserving a curse
challenge.explanation: Verse 24 concerns striking someone secretly, and verse 25 concerns harming an innocent person through bribery; both describe grave injustice condemned by the people.

questions.question: What does the phrase “an innocent person” mean in verse 25?
answers: A person who is not guilty and does not deserve punishment
A person who has washed his hands
Blood that has been washed with water
questions.explanation: An innocent person is someone who is not guilty and whose harm or death is unjustified.

questions.question: Why does the people say “Amen” after each curse?
answers: To ask forgiveness for the act
To publicly agree that the act deserves condemnation
To announce that the offender has been found
questions.explanation: Saying “Amen” expresses agreement with the curse and acceptance of the moral principle it represents.

questions.question: What detail do the two verses share, although each describes it differently?
answers: In both cases the offender acts on behalf of a court
In both cases the act is done for the poor
In both cases a person suffers serious harm, and the act is presented as deserving a curse
questions.explanation: Verse 24 concerns striking someone secretly, and verse 25 concerns harming an innocent person through bribery; both describe grave injustice condemned by the people.

paragraphs.title: Commitment to All the Words of the Law

easy.question: Who says “Amen” at the end of the verse?
answers: All the people
The priests alone
Moses alone
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And all the people shall say, Amen.”

easy.question: Who is called “cursed”?
answers: Anyone who teaches the Law
Anyone who does not uphold the words of the Law by doing them
All the people
easy.explanation: The curse is directed at anyone who does not keep the words of the Law in practice.

easy.question: What were the people required to do with the words of the Law?
answers: Keep them only in a book
Study them without obeying them
Uphold them and do them
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes not only the words of the Law but also the duty to uphold and practice them.

medium.question: What is the connection between failing to keep the Law and the word “cursed” in the verse?
answers: Failing to keep the Law brings a curse
Failing to keep the Law brings a blessing
There is no connection
medium.explanation: The word “cursed” introduces the warning against anyone who does not uphold the words of the Law.

medium.question: In the phrase “does not uphold the words of the Law,” what does “uphold” mean?
answers: Write down
Keep and practice
Speak aloud
medium.explanation: In the context of “to do them,” “uphold” means to keep, establish, and carry out the words of the Law.

medium.question: What is the order of ideas in the verse?
answers: The people say “Amen,” and then the curse is stated
The Law is written, and then the people study it
The curse is stated against anyone who does not keep the Law, and then the people answer “Amen”
medium.explanation: The verse begins with the curse against anyone who does not uphold the Law and ends with the people’s response, “Amen.”

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that all the people answer “Amen”?
answers: The people agree with and affirm the warning
The people are exempt from keeping the Law
The people do not understand the words
challenge.explanation: The response “Amen” expresses agreement with and approval of what was said.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that keeping the Law is not merely a matter of speaking?
answers: The word “all”
The words “to do them”
The word “Amen”
challenge.explanation: The words “to do them” emphasize that the Law must be put into practice.

challenge.question: Who is described by the phrase “anyone who” at the beginning of the verse?
answers: All the people who say “Amen”
The words of the Law alone
The person who does not uphold the words of the Law
challenge.explanation: The phrase introduces the person who is cursed: anyone who does not uphold the words of the Law.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that all the people answer “Amen”?
answers: The people agree with and affirm the warning
The people are exempt from keeping the Law
The people do not understand the words
questions.explanation: The response “Amen” expresses agreement with and approval of what was said.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that keeping the Law is not merely a matter of speaking?
answers: The word “all”
The words “to do them”
The word “Amen”
questions.explanation: The words “to do them” emphasize that the Law must be put into practice.

questions.question: Who is described by the phrase “anyone who” at the beginning of the verse?
answers: All the people who say “Amen”
The words of the Law alone
The person who does not uphold the words of the Law
questions.explanation: The phrase introduces the person who is cursed: anyone who does not uphold the words of the Law.
